topic: Const Iterators in C++ Standard Library Containers
explanation: In modern C++, containers such as std::set, std::map, and others provide iterators that are 'const' iterators, meaning they do not allow modification of the elements they point to. These iterators are used to traverse containers in a read-only manner, ensuring the integrity of the container’s elements and maintaining the container's invariants. Const iterators are essential for safe, non-modifying access to container elements, especially in contexts where data integrity and const-correctness are critical.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of const iterators (cbegin, cend, crbegin, crend) to traverse a std::set in a read-only manner. The iterators prevent modification of the container elements, ensuring data integrity. The code shows forward and reverse iteration using const iterators, exemplifying how C++ enforces const-correctness when accessing container elements, which is crucial for safe and predictable code in modern C++ programming.
